items.title: Iran talks in Qatar on a plan to reopen Hormuz, while tanker strikes continue
items.summary: Iran's top diplomat said negotiators are in Qatar discussing a proposal that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days, and a State Department official said the US remains open to talks but would change course if the Strait does not return to normal. Meanwhile the IRGC Navy said two oil tankers hit mines, and a Qatari LNG tanker was struck on Friday. Reports are from 1 November and some claims are unverified, so treat this as provisional.
items.why: A deal or a breakdown moves oil prices, which feed into corporate budgets, hiring and marketing spend.

items.title: Gaza aid cut: World Food Programme reduces support for 500,000 people
items.summary: Search results report the WFP cut aid to 500,000 Palestinians in Gaza citing funding shortages, and Gaza's Health Ministry says more than 1,570 people have been killed since the truce began. No Ukraine update dated today was found, so Ukraine is left out.
items.why: Funding-driven cuts show how donor budgets shape humanitarian operations and NGO hiring.
items.src: Search summary of Al Jazeera reporting

items.title: Rupee holds near 95 to 96 per dollar as RBI defends it and weighs remittance limits (reports from October)
items.summary: Business Standard market reports and CNBC (16 October) put the rupee around 95 to 96 per dollar with Brent near 95 dollars; the RBI has restricted rebooking of cancelled forex derivatives, and an ANC report says it is reportedly considering limits on overseas remittances, with education and healthcare exempt. S&P Global is cited seeing about 97 by end-2026. Nothing dated 2 November turned up and the sources vary in date, so treat the figures as provisional.
items.why: A weak rupee raises the cost of foreign education, imports and overseas plans, and squeezes company margins.

items.title: Sensex up 308 points to 74,459 and Nifty at 23,053 on Friday 30 October (3 days old)
items.summary: Business Standard's market close for 30 October shows the Sensex up 308.49 points (0.42%) to 74,459.53 and the Nifty 50 up 116.35 points (0.51%) to 23,053.10, led by IT shares. Elevated Brent crude remains a worry for inflation and the external accounts. Markets were shut on Sunday and no Monday session report was found yet.
items.why: Market sentiment shapes recruiters' risk appetite and campus-hiring plans.

items.title: US stocks fell as investors questioned Big Tech's heavy AI spending
items.summary: A search summary says US shares dropped after key earnings and inflation data, a day after the Federal Reserve held rates. No company figures were given, so this is a general market note only.
items.why: Shows how investor patience with AI spending can change tech hiring and ad budgets.

items.title: Google, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic back one robots.txt token to opt out of AI training
items.summary: Reports from 30 October say the four firms will honour a single robots.txt entry that lets sites block AI training crawlers. Anthropic has started, Microsoft plans 1 February 2027 and Google targets 2027. It covers training crawlers only, not every AI use of web content.
items.why: Content consent is becoming a brand and marketing-policy issue.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly trims its funding round to 20 billion dollars, with details conflicting
items.summary: One newsletter says the round was cut to 20 billion dollars at a 1.25 trillion dollar valuation from 30 billion at 1.4 trillion, and that OpenAI plans to buy Google's TPU chips. Another report in the same results gives different details, so all figures are provisional.
items.why: Investor appetite decides which AI vendors employers can rely on.

items.title: ChatGPT and Codex will share one token allowance from December
items.summary: A search summary says OpenAI confirmed on 31 October that from December ChatGPT and Codex will draw from a single shared token-based allowance for Plus, Pro and Business subscribers. It also lists Apple adding Alibaba's Qwen to Apple Intelligence in China, with a developer beta on 4 November; that item is unconfirmed.
items.why: Pricing changes show how AI products are being repackaged for subscribers.
